title: Swing curve: melee hitbox, trail and first-person arc aligned to the clip; spears and shortswords extend
player_outcome: What you see is what hits. The blade sweeps Terraria's overhead arc, from behind the head down in front, and the hit, the trail and the first-person arc all follow it with the same timing. The trail uses the weapon's colour and grows with size prefixes. Spear and shortsword heads visibly extend to the full reach of the hit.
design: Verified: MeleeSystem.Connects (MeleeSystem.cs:103-106) sweeps a horizontal arc linearly from tick 0. SwingTrail (SwingTrail.cs:92-95) matches it, while the clip winds up until t 0.22. MeleeSwingParams.TrailColor is never read.

New Core Gameplay/Entities/SwingCurve.cs evaluates keyed curves [(t, deg, ease)] with the same easing names as motion.tl (in, out, io, lin). The swing curve comes from GameWorld.Styles swing.bladeCurve. Default keys: t0 150° (behind/above), 0.2 165°, 0.46 0° (forward, strike), 0.62 −60° (low front), 1.0 −45°. A thrust curve (extension 0→1→0 with a hold) comes from rapier/spear 'extend'.

MeleeSystem swing plane: forward F is the aim yaw, U is world up, R = F×U. The plane is tilted by config planeTilt (15°) toward R. Pivot = Center + (0, 0.45, 0) + R·0.2. The blade direction at angle θ is cosθ·F + sinθ·U (tilted). Reach = swing.Length·CellSize·Prefixes.Size + 0.6.

Each tick, sample the blade segment between θ(t_prev) and θ(t) in ≤15° steps and test NPC volumes by distance from the box to the segment ≤ bladeHalfWidth (0.15) + lateralTolerance (config 0.5 m, for 3D forgiveness). Keep the point-blank rule. MeleeSwingParams.Arc scales the curve's angles about the strike angle by Arc/150.
Thrust hits only while extension ≥ 0.6 along the aim (the existing tolerance stays).
SwingTrail samples the same SwingCurve and plane to build the ribbon. Colour = Swing.TrailColor ?? rarity colour; width scales with Prefixes.Size. The thrust streak is 0.2 m wide with a tip sparkle.

PlayerAvatar and ViewModel: melee models are scaled so the model tip matches the hit reach, clamped 0.75–1.6. Spears and shortswords translate the held node along its axis by (reach − modelLength)·extension(t).
FP: ViewModel maps the blade angle from the same curve onto a camera-space rotation, so the FP arc equals the gameplay arc.

risks: Vertical-plane hits may feel less forgiving than the old horizontal sweep; lateralTolerance and planeTilt are data-tunable.
